currentContext.expansion: The Company's principal expansion project is a greenfield EHV Power Transformer manufacturing facility. Under 'Update on Capex' the Directors state that construction of the greenfield EHV Power Transformer manufacturing facility is getting completed as per schedule, with completion targeted by June 2026, subject to unforeseen circumstances. Under 'Strategic Focus and Capacity Planning' management adds that the new capacity for power transformers is expected to be operational from July 2026 and will be partly utilized during the year, a phased ramp-up that will support higher production volumes and strengthen the Company's ability to scale operations. Separately, the Board of Directors at its meeting held on May 05, 2026 approved an investment of Rs 25 crores for acquisition of a new plot of land near Vadodara, to keep a land bank ready for future use. The Directors' Report also notes that a state-of-the-art new manufacturing facility is being developed, in which Hetrich Germany VPD and battery-operated trollies will be among the advanced features. Capacity utilization surpassed 100% for the second year in a row during FY2025-26, and sales volume rose to 16,514 MVA from 15,460 MVA. On the energy side the Company added a 600 KW solar installation at its Jarod unit. Industry-wide, management observes that several major players have announced significant expansion and capital expenditure plans to scale up production capacities for both power and distribution transformers over the next few years, and expects margins to normalize as that capacity lands.

themes.title: Transformer & grid-component shortage
themes.need: Transformer makers are running flat-out at record order books even as core-capacity ramps land (ATLANTAELE 16k->63k MVA, Q1FY27 record order book INR3,117cr on record INR972cr quarterly inflow, Vadod now PGCIL 400kV-approved with a 765kV tech tie-up in final talks; TARIL toward 75k+ MVA, Q1FY27 UEOB INR6,630cr +26% YoY on a >INR1,000cr single-shot PGCIL Ultra-Mega order, though a Changodar-expansion air-pocket held Q1 revenue to +10%; SHILCTECH adding 220kV) yet the binding constraint is still everything INSIDE a transformer - CRGO core steel, CTC/winding wire (KSHINTL/BHAGYANGR), bushings/insulators (YASHHV; 18-24mo lead, ~95% RIP/OIP imported) and transformer oil (APARINDS); both OEMs are now backward-integrating to own the bottleneck (TARIL's INR900-1,000cr CRGO/CTC/bushing/pressboard programme). Capacity-gated supply is the repeated 'need of the hour' and is driving pricing power now, though both OEMs flagged ~60,000 MVA of new 400kV capacity landing industry-wide in 3-4 months as a 1-year-out overcapacity watch-item (neither sees pricing pressure yet).
themes.driver: PGCIL Ultra-Mega order conversion (TARIL's first >INR1,000cr single-shot award) + Vadod/Changodar capacity ramps; 400kV short-circuit tests and 765kV PGCIL approvals due by Q2FY27-end are the next re-rating triggers; TARIL's Changodar restart (Aug-2026) is the swing quarter for its own growth reacceleration.
